text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Classification company Det Norske Veritas says some shipowners shift to less serious classification companies when their vessels become 20 years old and are up for a thorough inspection.
- Explorer Borge Ousland came home to Oslo on Wednesday after becoming the first person ever to cross the South Pole alone and without assistance.

- Offshore services company Petroleum Geo-Services ASA (PGS) says it made record earnings in 1996 and completed its first five years in business as a leader in the marine seismic industry. PGS booked $91 million in operating profits against $58 million in 1995.

- Den norske Bank ASA (DNB), Norway's biggest commercial bank, announced 1996 net profits of 2.70 billion crowns, 1.7 percent higher than in 1995. The bank attributed the result to cost cuts and to the healthy Norwegian economy.
- DNB says it wants to be in the forefront in the restructuring of the Norwegian financial community and expects mergers to take place this year.
- Power producer Hafslund ASA posted full-year operating profits of 274 million crowns against 265 million crowns in the corresponding 1995 period.
